title: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022
note: Manually transcribed against every page of the 12-page supplied study PDF. Green answer-cell highlights are recorded as supplied marks, not certified official answers. Questions are sorted by printed number; page values retain actual study-PDF order, which is not fully numerical. Spelling, capitalization and units are lightly normalized without changing option order.

questions.prompt: Which muscle contraction makes the pleural pressure more positive?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Contraction of the expiratory internal intercostals raises pleural pressure. The inspiratory muscles expand the thorax.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 1; source page 2.

questions.prompt: According to V/Q mismatch, what is the difference between the oxygen pressure of the lower, middle and upper alveoli in a healthy upright subject?
options: Oxygen pressure in the lower alveoli is higher than the middle and upper
Oxygen pressure in the upper alveoli is higher than the middle and lower
Oxygen pressure in the middle alveoli is higher than the lower and upper
Oxygen pressure is the same in all alveoli
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The apex has the highest V/Q ratio because perfusion falls more steeply than ventilation; alveolar PO2 is consequently higher there.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 2; source page 2.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of pleural pressure changes on alveolar pressure during inspiration?
options: The more negative the pleural pressure, the more positive the alveolar pressure
The more positive the pleural pressure, the more positive the alveolar pressure
The more positive the pleural pressure, the more negative the alveolar pressure
The more negative the pleural pressure, the more negative the alveolar pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: During inspiratory airflow, falling pleural pressure expands the lungs and lowers alveolar pressure below atmospheric pressure. This describes the inspiratory phase, not a universal proportional relation; alveolar pressure returns to atmospheric at end inspiration.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 3; source page 2.

questions.prompt: If in a premature infant the size of the alveoli is one-third of normal and surface tension is tripled due to low surfactant production, how does the collapse pressure change compared with a normal infant?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: By the spherical Laplace approximation P=2T/r, tripling tension and reducing radius to one-third multiplies collapse pressure by nine.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 4; source page 5.

questions.prompt: If lung compliance and thoracic compliance are equal, each 300 mL/cmH2O, what is total pulmonary-system compliance in mL/cmH2O?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reciprocal compliances add: 1/Ctotal=1/300+1/300, so Ctotal=150 mL/cmH2O.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 5; source page 5.

questions.prompt: What part of the lung in an upright subject has zone 2 blood flow during exercise?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the simplified exercise model used by the paper, increased pulmonary vascular pressure converts apical zone 2 to continuous zone 3 flow. The answer is model-dependent; actual zones depend on vascular and alveolar pressures.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 6; source page 4.

questions.prompt: The diffusion coefficient of a gas in a liquid depends on which factor?
options: Pressure difference between the two ends of the diffusion path
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The diffusion coefficient is proportional to gas solubility and inversely proportional to the square root of molecular weight. The other options affect diffusion rate through geometry or the pressure gradient.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 7; source page 4.

questions.prompt: If the thickness of the respiratory membrane doubles due to pulmonary fibrosis, what will the CO2 diffusing capacity be, approximately?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Doubling thickness halves diffusing capacity. The supplied answer assumes the conventional resting CO2 diffusing capacity of about 400-450 mL/min/mmHg, giving about 200-225; 200 is the nearest offered value. This unstated reference assumption is essential.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 8; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which statement is NOT correct about anatomical shunt?
options: Oxygen pressure decreases from 104 to 95 mmHg
Arterial blood CO2 pressure increases from 40 to 45 mmHg
Pulmonary vein and bronchial vein blood are mixed
It forms part of the physiological shunt
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Normal venous admixture reduces systemic arterial PO2 below ideal end-capillary PO2. It does not raise normal arterial PCO2 to the mixed-venous value of 45 mmHg.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 9; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Inhibition of beta receptors in the airways leads to an increase in which of the following?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Beta2 activation relaxes airway smooth muscle; inhibiting this effect favors bronchoconstriction and increased airway resistance.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 10; source page 3.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the Haldane effect in the respiratory system?
options: It increases the release of O2 from hemoglobin
It increases the excretion of CO2 from the lungs
It reduces the tendency of Fe2+ in hemoglobin to bind oxygen
It reduces the diffusion of CO2 from peripheral tissue into the capillaries
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Oxygenation of hemoglobin decreases CO2 carriage and releases buffered H+, assisting CO2 unloading in the lungs.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 11; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which respiratory center provides strong signals for contraction of rectus abdominis to increase pulmonary ventilation during deep expiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Ventral respiratory neurons recruit abdominal and other expiratory muscles during forceful ventilation.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 12; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What is the initial pressure difference for O2 diffusion from alveoli into pulmonary capillaries?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the paper's sea-level reference values, alveolar PO2 is 104 and entering mixed-venous PO2 is 40 mmHg: the initial gradient is 64 mmHg.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 13; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of using acetazolamide, an inhibitor of carbonic anhydrase, on respiratory gases?
options: A decrease in arterial blood O2 pressure
An increase in O2 pressure in interstitial fluid
A decrease in arterial blood CO2 pressure
An increase in CO2 pressure in interstitial fluid
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Unresolved single-best answer: the scan marks D, consistent with tissue CO2 retention during substantial acute carbonic-anhydrase inhibition. Oral acetazolamide can also lower arterial PCO2 through metabolic acidosis and increased ventilation (C). Dose, timing and experimental context are omitted, so the supplied mark is preserved but not graded.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 14; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the pneumotaxic center in regulation of respiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the paper's simplified center model, pontine input terminates the dorsal inspiratory ramp. C is the intended shorthand for inspiratory switch-off; the modern network is more distributed.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 15; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which factor does NOT stimulate the chemosensitive area in the medulla?
options: Increased H+ concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid
Increased CO2 concentration in interstitial fluid of the medulla
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Low arterial PO2 mainly stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors. CO2 crosses into brain fluids and generates H+, stimulating central chemosensitive neurons.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 16; source page 7.

questions.prompt: In histology, in which part of the nasal cavity are goblet cells observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Goblet cells are a standard population in nasal respiratory epithelium. Source spelling is normalized; option order is preserved.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 17; source page 7.

questions.prompt: In which part of the air ducts is true elastic fiber observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The supplied mark is D, probably referring to elastic fibers of the true vocal ligament. As written, the stem only asks about elastic fibers, which also occur in tracheal and bronchial walls; it does not uniquely identify the larynx.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 18; source page 7.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the macrophage in lung tissue?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Alveolar macrophages are also called dust cells. Clara cells are now called club cells and are secretory epithelial cells.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 19; source page 8.

questions.prompt: In which part of the lung are Clara cells observed?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Clara, now club, cells characterize bronchiolar epithelium.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 20; source page 8.

questions.prompt: Which alveolar cell has a circular nucleus and granules in its cytoplasm?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Type II pneumocytes are cuboidal with rounded nuclei and surfactant-containing lamellar bodies. The source's 'nuclease' is normalized to nucleus.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 21; source page 8.

questions.prompt: The nasal septum consists of all of the following except:
options: Perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The lacrimal bone contributes to the lateral nasal wall; septal cartilage, vomer and the ethmoid perpendicular plate contribute to the septum.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 22; source page 9.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements about the maxillary sinus are correct except:
options: The roof of the sinus forms the floor of the orbit
The maxillary sinus opens into the middle meatus
It is the largest paranasal sinus
The floor of the maxillary sinus is related to the sphenopalatine foramen
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The sinus floor relates to the alveolar process and upper teeth. The sphenopalatine foramen is a posterior nasal gateway, not a floor relation.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 23; source page 9.

questions.prompt: The posterior inferior nasal nerve is a branch of which nerve?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Posterior inferior lateral nasal branches arise through the greater palatine nerve pathway.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 24; source page 9.

questions.prompt: All of the following cartilages have articular facets except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The epiglottis does not participate in the synovial cricothyroid or cricoarytenoid joints. The clear answer-cell highlight is C; a separate horizontal pen stroke near B is not treated as a second key.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 25; source page 10.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements about the larynx are correct except:
options: The middle cavity of the larynx is limited above by vestibular folds
The middle cavity of the larynx expands laterally into a ventricle
The laryngeal saccule opens into the vestibule
Mucous glands in the saccules lubricate the vocal folds
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The saccule extends upward from the laryngeal ventricle, rather than opening directly into the vestibule.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 26; source page 10.

questions.prompt: All of the following attach to the arytenoid cartilage except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The arytenoid provides attachment for vocal and vestibular structures and the quadrangular membrane; it has no direct hyoid attachment.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 27; source page 10.

questions.prompt: All of the following arteries supply the nasal cavity except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Internal-carotid supply reaches the nose through ophthalmic and ethmoidal branches. Superior labial and greater palatine branches contribute; the superior thyroid artery does not normally supply the nasal cavity.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 28; source page 11.

questions.prompt: All of the following nerves innervate the nasal cavity except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Olfaction uses CN I and general sensation uses V1/V2. The recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies the larynx, not the nasal cavity.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 29; source page 11.

questions.prompt: What forms the anterior margin of the laryngeal inlet?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The epiglottis forms the anterior inlet margin; aryepiglottic folds form its lateral boundaries.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 30; source page 11.

questions.prompt: The left lung is related to all of the following structures except:
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The azygos arch passes over the right lung root. The spleen is an inferior relation of the left lung through the diaphragm; the esophagus and thoracic aorta are medial relations.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 31; source page 11.

questions.prompt: In surface anatomy, at which rib is the pleural shadow in the midaxillary line?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The inferior pleural reflection is at approximately rib 10 in the midaxillary line; the lung border is two ribs higher.

evidence: Respiratory final exam — July 4, 2022; printed question 32; source page 12.

questions.prompt: The cartilaginous, muscular and connective-tissue components of the trachea and lungs derive from which tissue surrounding the foregut?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: No unambiguous answer-cell highlight is visible in the scan. The audited answer is A: splanchnic mesoderm forms these supporting tissues, while endoderm forms the airway epithelium and glands.

questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: The course account gives about 17 prenatal branching generations by the end of the sixth month. The Persian numerals in the scan were visually read as 12, 6, 17 and 4.
